title: Homolytic vs Heterolytic Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Two friends share two sweets: each takes one, or one grabs both. Aarav knows a covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons, so when a bond breaks, who keeps the two electrons? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) we see both ways a bond breaks, and how nucleophiles and electrophiles attack.

On the molecule bench, a curved arrow carries the C-Br pair onto bromine: bromide leaves and a flat sp2 carbocation is left behind (heterolytic fission). Chlorine in sunlight splits fairly with two fish hook arrows into free radicals (homolytic fission), and a carbanion keeps its lone pair. We build the stability order of carbocations, free radicals and carbanions step by step, then a hydroxide nucleophile attacks a carbocation electrophile along a curved arrow to form a new bond. A worked example sorts four species, then an exam trap, an original exam pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 83 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
